title: F319/F320 fallout: a check whose reason is false, and the wiring's fail modes
desiredOutcome: check-prohibitions asks the property it wants -- does this hook emit a permission decision -- instead of reading py-launch.sh's no-interpreter fail mode as a proxy for it, with the token/property agreement itself asserted; and SECURITY.md's per-hook fail-mode table is compared to hooks.json's wiring in both directions by a gate, so a table that tells a security reader a blocking guard fails silently cannot ship. The reported .env evasion is NOT in scope: it does not reproduce in this tree or in v2.2.0, and the liveness half is F320.

tasks.title: A check may not read a fail mode as a proxy for the property it wants
tasks.description: F319. deciding_bash_hooks() filters to the 'ask' registrations and states as its reason that a hook launched 'open' CANNOT return a permission decision. Driven through py-launch.sh with an interpreter present, that is false: token=ask, token=open and no token all yield permissionDecision=deny. The token is py-launch.sh's no-interpreter fail mode (mode=${2:-open}) and gates nothing once an interpreter exists. The filter still selects the right set, because the wiring assigns 'ask' to precisely the PreToolUse hooks that decide -- so this is a correct answer resting on a proxy while stating the proxy is the property. Ask it directly instead: does this hook's source emit a permissionDecision, read via AST so a mention in a comment does not count, since driving journal-writes.py to find out would make a read-only check write the audit trail it is checking. Then assert the derived set and the wiring's ask set AGREE, so a deciding guard registered 'open' becomes a finding here rather than a silent weakening.

outcome.technical: deciding_bash_hooks() filtered on py-launch.sh's no-interpreter fail-mode token and wrote as its reason that a hook launched `open` cannot return a permission decision; driven through the launcher with an interpreter present, ask/open/none all yield deny. It now asks the property via AST (emits_decision) and fail_mode_drift() binds token to property in both directions, gated in main(). prove-gates rows added and proven both ways.
outcome.descriptive: A check no longer rests on a proxy while stating the proxy is the property.

tasks.title: SECURITY.md's fail-mode table is compared to the wiring it describes
tasks.description: F319. SECURITY.md's 'Fail modes (by design)' table describes, per hook and per event, what happens when py-launch.sh finds no interpreter -- a fact hooks.json owns and SECURITY.md itself names as the authority. Nothing in the tree reads that table: no file under tools/, scripts/ or tests/ mentions the column or parses it. It is accurate today, so this adds the thing that would catch drift rather than repairing drift. Consequence of drift is not a stale doc: it is SECURITY.md telling a reader that a blocking guard fails silently, or that a silent hook prompts, at the moment they decide whether to trust the plugin with a threat model. Three directions: a row disagreeing with its registration's token; a wired (hook, event) pair no row describes, without which deleting a row makes the table agree with itself; and 'ask' on any event but PreToolUse, where no permission-decision channel exists. The parse must survive a cell wording two events (journal-writes) and a parenthetical disambiguator (require-plan (state commit)), or it under-reports silently.

outcome.technical: gate-parity.failmode_table_drift() compares SECURITY.md's per-hook fail-mode table to hooks.json, reading the loud token, the default mode and the decision event OFF py-launch.sh rather than restating them; multi-event cells and parenthetical disambiguators parsed; a wired pair no row describes, a row nothing wires, a loud mode on a non-decision event and an unlaunched registration are all findings. Wired into parity()/render() so the gate exits 1.
outcome.descriptive: The security document's fail-mode table is checked against the wiring it describes.

tasks.title: F302's narrowing stops excusing real failures and starts firing for pre-commit
tasks.description: F323: the 128+N arm rests on summary_count knowing four output shapes, so mocha --reporter json records 139 real failures as could-not-run; and ran_count counts lines for _STEP_WORDS so the arm never fires for pre-commit, which is the shape F302 was reported against.

outcome.technical: reached_a_verdict(text, command) + _END_OF_RUN asks whether the runner reached its own last line - a weaker question than the counting readers, so reporters they cannot parse (mocha json/xunit, nunit, checkstyle) grade as failed rather than could-not-run, and _STEP_WORDS runners (pre-commit) are reachable. TAP's plan line is anchored to end-of-output so the classic plan-first form no longer counts as ended; composite runners answer False. Residual direction named in the docstring: an unknown shape falls toward could-not-run, never toward green.
outcome.descriptive: A killed runner is could-not-run for every reporter shape, and real failures are never excused as crashes.

tasks.title: A byte-precise build input carries an end-of-line contract
tasks.description: BUG-4: scripts/ui/* are byte-precise build inputs read with newline='' on purpose, because the assembled UI_HTML/_CSS/_SCRIPT byte-identity depends on exact bytes. With no .gitattributes a windows checkout under autocrlf rewrites them to CRLF, so every pin spanning a line boundary fails. tasks.title: The tree-wide lints memoise the default tree, the way _scan_edges already does
tasks.description: Operator asked for the plugin to be faster and cheaper, not only more correct. Profiled with cProfile: test__deps.py is ~70% of the sweep's wall clock at 12 workers, and its time is config_key_reads and dict_key_contracts re-parsing every module per call (dozens of calls per run over a tree that cannot change), while test__output's hottest function is _tokenize, entered several times per line because neighbours are re-tokenized. Repair follows the _scan_edges precedent exactly: default-tree-only memo, fixture callers bypass it, answers copied on the way out, with the mm2/mm3 case pair (memo in use; fixture not served) for each new memo, and a bounded LRU on the pure tokenizer.

outcome.technical: Profiled with cProfile: test__deps.py bounded the sweep's wall clock and spent it in config_key_reads re-parsing every module per call (dozens of calls, two of them hitting a first memo that bypassed on any explicit vocabulary); test__output's hottest function was _tokenize, entered several times per line. config_key_reads is memoised for the default tree keyed by vocabulary (frozensets, hashable as-is), copied on the way out, fixtures bypass; _tokenize sits behind functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096), pure and never mutated by a caller. Five-case pair per memo mirroring mm0-mm4; a dict_key_contracts memo was tried and removed because it hit once in fourteen calls. Measured in a scratch copy: test__deps 18.3s -> 12.7s, test__output 9.7s -> 8.9s, _tokenize 643k -> 139k calls; re-derive rather than trust these.
outcome.descriptive: The two suites that bound every sweep and every CI run got measurably faster, with the memo proven honest.

tasks.title: The plan gate says an uncovered file is uncovered once per session, not on every edit
tasks.description: F355, field report 8. The warn tier emits the same verbatim paragraph on EVERY Edit/Write of an uncovered file and asks the model to relay it, so an operator doing non-phase work reads it dozens of times an afternoon (this session: ~15 relays). The decision is unchanged; only the advisory's frequency is: the first edit of a file speaks the paragraph, later edits of the SAME file in the same session emit one short line naming the count, a different file speaks again. Per-session file state already exists in the gate's state file. Red-first both ways: a repeat edit must not carry the paragraph; a new file must.

outcome.technical: require-plan's warn tier consults plan-gate-warned-<sid>.json (the _owner_note throttle shape, under the plan-gate- prefix GC sweeps): first edit of an uncovered file speaks the paragraph with the relay instruction, a later edit of the same file returns one line, a different file speaks again; Pre reads, Post writes. The gate EVENT is still appended on every edit - only the relay text is throttled - and the decision is untouched. Driven on the live path as Claude Code drives it. Observed: the hook firing on this checkout's own edits is the installed 2.0.1 cache copy, not this file (F320).
outcome.descriptive: An operator doing non-phase work reads the uncovered-file advisory once per file, not on every edit.
